parts.name: Right upper lobe
parts.info: Three segments: apical, posterior and anterior. It reaches up above the collarbone.
parts.fact: Inhaled objects and tuberculosis often settle in the upper lobes.

parts.name: Right middle lobe
parts.info: The smallest lobe, found only on the right. It has a lateral and a medial segment.
parts.fact: The left lung has the lingula instead of a middle lobe.

parts.name: Right lower lobe
parts.info: The largest lobe, with five segments resting on the diaphragm.
parts.fact: Food or fluid breathed in while lying down most often reaches the lower lobes.

parts.name: Left upper lobe
parts.info: Includes the lingula, a tongue-shaped part that matches the right middle lobe.

parts.name: Left lower lobe
parts.info: Four or five segments resting on the diaphragm behind the heart.
parts.fact: The left lung is about 10% smaller than the right, to make room for the heart.

parts.name: Trachea
parts.info: The windpipe. A 10–12 cm tube that carries air from the throat to the lungs.
parts.fact: It splits at the carina into the two main bronchi, about level with the second rib.

parts.name: Cartilage rings
parts.info: C-shaped rings of cartilage that keep the trachea and main bronchi open while you breathe.
parts.fact: The open back of each 'C' lets the oesophagus bulge forward when you swallow.

parts.name: Main bronchi
parts.info: The two branches of the trachea, one to each lung.
parts.fact: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical, so inhaled objects usually go right.

parts.name: Bronchial tree
parts.info: Lobar and segmental bronchi branching inside each lobe. Slice or hide the lobes to see them.
parts.fact: The airways branch about 23 times between the trachea and the air sacs.

parts.name: Pulmonary arteries
parts.info: Bring oxygen-poor blood from the heart to the lungs. Shown in blue because the blood is low in oxygen.
parts.fact: They follow the bronchi, branch for branch, into every segment.

parts.name: Pulmonary veins
parts.info: Carry freshly oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium. Shown in red.
parts.fact: Unlike the arteries, they run between segments rather than alongside the bronchi.
